title: Skeletal and orofacial muscle responses to tooth-borne and tooth-bone-borne rapid palatal expansion: a short-term prospective CBCT and ultrasound elastography study
abstractText: Abstract Objective To compare transverse skeletal changes and orofacial muscle stiffness following tooth-borne rapid palatal expansion (TB-RPE) and tooth-bone-borne RPE (TBB-RPE) using a combined cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and ultrasonographic elastography (UE) approach. Materials and Methods Twenty-four adolescents with transverse maxillary deficiency were treated with TB-RPE (n = 12) or TBB-RPE (n = 12). CBCT scans were obtained at baseline (T0) and after active expansion (T1) as part of routine clinical assessment to evaluate skeletal changes. UE, including strain elastography (SE) and shear-wave elastography (SWE), was performed for the masseter, temporalis, geniohyoid, and anterior digastric muscles. Results Both groups exhibited significant transverse skeletal expansion without significant between-group differences in midpalatal or pterygopalatine suture separation, or maxillary and nasal width changes (p > 0.05). Muscle thickness remained stable. SE values increased in several muscles in both groups, whereas SWE values showed variable changes; however, no significant intergroup differences were observed, except for two isolated reductions in the TB-RPE group. Conclusion TB-RPE and TBB-RPE produced comparable short-term skeletal expansion and similar elastographic muscle responses. Early musculoskeletal adaptations during active expansion appear independent of anchorage design. Clinical Relevance In adolescents, appliance selection for rapid palatal expansion may be guided primarily by skeletal considerations, as short-term neuromuscular responses do not differ significantly between tooth-borne and tooth-bone-borne designs.

title: Cardiovascular complications and cardiovascular death are rare in severe COVID-19 presenting with myocardial injury or failure
abstractText: Abstract SARS-COV2 infection has been linked to cardiovascular complications. Published data suggest that cardiac injury may be a common disease feature and contribute to morbidity and mortality in severe COVID-19. Since early in the pandemic, little data has emerged describing what cardiovascular complications arise from myocardial injury in severe COVID-19 and whether these complications contribute to mortality. We set out to describe the incidence and nature of cardiovascular complications in patients with severe COVID-19 infection and biochemical or imaging evidence of myocardial injury. We analyzed consecutive patients admitted for severe COVID-19 and presenting with biochemical or echocardiographic evidence of myocardial injury across 16 centers within the CARDIO-COVID investigator-initiated consortium. A light-GBM machine learning model was used to identify variables associated with mortality. Our study included 1,328 patients. ICU mortality was 29.4%. Factors most associated with mortality were age, SOFA Cardiovascular score, elevated troponin, intubation, high vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS), high PEEP, and high FiO2. Individual cardiovascular (myocardial infarction, stroke, pulmonary embolism, myocarditis, VT/VF, new onset heart failure) complications were rare (all < 5%) but common in sum (17.6%), and did not present significant association with mortality. Patients with high VIS and SOFA Cardiovascular scores had a significantly higher incidence of secondary bacterial pneumonias suggesting septic shock played a role in their physiology. Investigator-adjudicated cause of death data identified respiratory failure and septic shock as primary causes of mortality. Though cardiovascular complications of severe COVID-19 are common, they do not seem to contribute significantly to mortality. Elevated cardiac enzymes and myocardial dysfunction carry prognostic value likely reflecting myocardial strain in the setting of multisystem organ dysfunction rather than direct myocardial injury by SARS-CoV2.

title: Association between serum uric acid-to-creatinine ratio and all-cause mortality in patients with coronary heart disease
abstractText: Abstract Background The serum uric acid-to-creatinine ratio (UCR), an indicator of renal function, has been linked to adverse cardiovascular outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the association between UCR and the risk of all-cause mortality in patients with coronary heart disease (CHD). Methods This longitudinal cohort study included patients with CHD who were admitted to the First Affiliated Hospital of Shantou University Medical College between January 2020 and April 2024. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, multivariate Cox regression models, and threshold effect analyses were used to assess the association between UCR and mortality risk. Results A total of 5,850 patients with CHD were included, with a mean age of 66.5 ± 10.9 years. During a median follow-up period of 487.5 days (interquartile range [IQR]: 240–833), 501 (8.6%) deaths occurred. RCS analysis revealed a U-shaped relationship between UCR and all-cause mortality risk, with patients having a UCR range of 3.5 to 6.5 showing the lowest mortality risk. Multivariate Cox regression models indicated that patients with UCR < 3.5 had a 46% higher mortality risk (HR = 1.46, 95% CI: 1.18–1.81), while those with UCR ≥ 6.5 had a 56% higher mortality risk (HR = 1.56, 95% CI: 1.13–2.15). A negative association between UCR and all-cause mortality risk was observed in patients with UCR < 4.418 (HR = 0.77, 95% CI: 0.68–0.88), whereas a positive association was observed in those with UCR ≥ 4.418 (HR = 1.21, 95% CI: 1.06–1.38). Conclusion A U-shaped relationship was observed between UCR and all-cause mortality risk in patients with CHD. The findings suggest that UCR may serve as a prognostic indicator of CHD.

title: Suitable organic fertilizer substitution improves grain yield and water use efficiency of rainfed maize by optimizing the water consumption structure on the Loess Plateau
abstractText: Limited and uneven precipitation constrains maize production and water use efficiency (WUE) in the rainfed Loess Plateau. Organic fertilizer substitution reduces inorganic fertilizer inputs, but its effects on yield formation through stage-specific water consumption remain unclear. A field experiment was conducted from 2021 to 2024 within a long-term trial established in 2016 under the fully mulched ridge-furrow system. Treatments comprised 0% (T1), 50.0% (T2), 37.5% (T3), 25.0% (T4), and 12.5% (T5) organic fertilizer N substitution and a no-fertilizer control (T6); T1–T5 received 200 kg N ha-1. T3 achieved a four-year mean grain yield of 7129.2 kg ha-1, 12.88%–29.00% higher than the other substitution treatments, comparable to T1, and with the lowest yield variability. Its WUE reached 24.85 kg ha-1 mm-1, exceeding the other substitution treatments by 17.27%–33.82%. In 2021 and 2022, pre-sowing soil water storage under T3 was 9.19%–10.59% higher than selected fertilized treatments. Mean total water consumption was 290.3 mm and did not differ among fertilized treatments. However, T3 reduced the proportion consumed during early vegetative growth and increased that during R1–R3. T3 also maintained relatively high kernel number and 1000-kernel weight and a relatively high source-sink ratio. Structural equation modeling showed that silking to the milk stage (R1–R3) water consumption affected yield mainly through kernel number, whereas pre-sowing soil water storage acted mainly through 1000-kernel weight. Overall, 37.5% organic fertilizer N substitution maintained a favorable pre-sowing soil water status, optimizing water consumption structure by decreasing vegetative growth stage water consumption and increasing R1–R3 water consumption without increasing total water consumption, coordinating sink capacity with post-silking assimilate supply, thus improving WUE, and increasing grain yield.

title: Effects of taekwondo match-simulated fatigue on static and dynamic balance performance in female athletes
abstractText: Abstract Background Balance is an important aspect of physical performance in taekwondo and can be affected by the high-intensity, intermittent, and repetitive movements performed during competition. This study investigated the effects of a taekwondo match-simulated fatigue protocol, designed to reproduce the intermittent kicking demands of competition, on static and dynamic balance performance in trained female taekwondo athletes. Methods Eighteen trained female taekwondo athletes completed a single-group repeated-measures study. Static and dynamic single-leg balance were measured on the dominant leg at rest and during testing initiated within one minute following completion of a taekwondo-specific match-simulation protocol using the Biodex Balance System. The protocol consisted of three 2-minute rounds, each separated by a 1-minute rest. Each round included repeated 10-second maximal-effort kicking bouts alternated with 10-second low-intensity bouncing recovery periods. Balance was assessed using the Overall, Anteroposterior, and Mediolateral Stability Indices. Separate 2 × 2 repeated-measures ANOVAs were conducted to examine the main effects of time and task condition, as well as their interaction, with partial eta squared (η²ₚ) reported as the effect-size measure. Results No significant main effects of time or task condition and no significant time × task condition interactions were found for the overall, anteroposterior, or mediolateral stability indices. Conclusions In trained female taekwondo athletes, a non-contact taekwondo match-simulation protocol did not result in statistically significant changes in single-leg static or dynamic balance performance, as measured by the Biodex Balance System during testing initiated within one minute post-protocol. These results are specific to this sample, the exercise protocol, and the assessment method, and should not be generalized to actual competition settings, other populations, or alternative testing conditions. Interpretation should be cautious due to the small sample size, absence of a control group, and lack of physiological or perceptual measures of fatigue. It remains unclear whether the findings indicate fatigue resistance or an insufficiently fatiguing protocol. Trial registration The trial was retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov with registration number (NCT07747064) and date (20260725).

title: Strategi Geoekonomi dan Dinamika Sistem Politik: Analisis Perbandingan Singapura dan Thailand dalam Perspektif David Easton
abstractText: Artikel ini menganalisis perbandingan strategi geoekonomi Singapura dan Thailand serta hubungannya dengan dinamika sistem politik. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode studi pustaka untuk mengkaji strategi perdagangan internasional, investasi asing, pengembangan industri, dan konektivitas ekonomi kedua negara. Analisis dilakukan menggunakan teori sistem politik David Easton (1965) melalui empat unsur sistem politik, yaitu input, proses konversi, output, dan feedback. Hasil pembahasan menunjukkan bahwa Singapura mengandalkan perdagangan global, investasi asing, serta infrastruktur pelabuhan dan logistik untuk mempertahankan daya saing internasional. Thailand lebih berfokus pada industri manufaktur, khususnya otomotif, ekspor, dan konektivitas regional. Kedua negara menghadapi tantangan dalam mempertahankan daya saing dan memperluas manfaat pembangunan. Kajian ini menegaskan bahwa keberhasilan strategi geoekonomi tidak hanya ditentukan oleh pertumbuhan perdagangan dan investasi, tetapi juga oleh kemampuan pemerintah mengevaluasi kebijakan, memperkuat kapasitas domestik, dan mendorong pemerataan manfaat ekonomi.

title: Sistem Pendukung Keputusan Akuisisi Sistem Informasi Desa Kedungwringin Menggunakan Metode Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP)
abstractText: Village digital transformation requires selecting an appropriate Village Information System (SID) acquisition model that aligns with the operational capabilities and budget of village apparatus. However, decision-makers at Kedungwringin Village Hall face difficulties in choosing between free open-source platforms (OpenSID), commercial cloud subscriptions (Vendor SaaS), and custom software development (Custom Development). This study aims to determine the optimal SID acquisition alternative using the Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) approach through the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) method. Data were collected through interviews and a Saaty-scale (1-9) pairwise comparison questionnaire completed twice by three key village stakeholders selected through purposive sampling; the second round was used as the main data. Multi-respondent preferences were aggregated using the geometric mean across five evaluation criteria: Cost Efficiency, Data Integration Capability, Data Security, Ease of Use, and Vendor Support. The results indicate that Ease of Use holds the highest priority weight (31.56%), followed by Data Security (21.09%), Data Integration Capability (18.51%), Vendor Support (14.44%), and Cost Efficiency (14.40%). The aggregated matrix met the consistency threshold (CR = 0.0322), although the individual matrices of all three respondents remained above 0.10 (0.233; 0.138; 0.143). Final synthesis ranks Custom Development first with a composite score of 51.40%, followed by OpenSID (24.92%) and Vendor SaaS (23.69%); the first rank remained stable in the sensitivity tests. The implication suggests that custom-built systems must be accompanied by source code handover agreements to avoid vendor lock-in.

title: Resenha: Adorno - Introdução à Dialética
abstractText: Publicado no Brasil em 2022, o livro Introdução à dialética é a transcrição de um curso de 20 aulas ministradas por Theodor Adorno em 1958. São abordados pelo filósofo dois tipos essenciais de dialética: a idealista, formulada sobretudo por G. Hegel, e a materialista, de origem ligada a K. Marx. Nesta resenha, chamo atenção para dois aspectos do pensamento de Adorno que são relevantes em debates contemporâneos, inclusive na Geografia: (i) a dialética como combate à reificação do pensamento e ao “pensar administrativo”, e (ii) o papel do pensamento crítico no combate a uma postura conformista e resignada.

title: Lefebvre, homem de periferia, esclarece Tempo de Equívocos
abstractText: This is a review of Le temps des méprises, a Henri Lefebvre’s book-length interview, translated into Portuguese as Tempo de equívocos by Pedro Denski and Sérgio Martins. It offers an exceptional critical account of the twentieth century, one that clearly resonates in the twenty-first century as well.

title: Diseminasi Teh Herbal Daun Sungkai (Peronema canescens Jack) melalui Edukasi Masyarakat pada Car Free Day Kota Padang
abstractText: Diseminasi hasil pengolahan tanaman lokal memerlukan kegiatan edukasi yang menjelaskan proses penyiapan bahan dan penyeduhan kepada masyarakat. Pengabdian ini bertujuan memperkenalkan teh herbal daun sungkai (Peronema canescens Jack) melalui edukasi langsung, leaflet, dan contoh produk pada kegiatan car free day di Padang. Kegiatan dilaksanakan pada 11 Agustus 2024 di kawasan GOR H. Agus Salim. Evaluasi dilakukan secara deskriptif melalui penelaahan laporan pelaksanaan, daftar hadir, jadwal, rincian pengadaan, serta dokumentasi produk. Daftar hadir memuat 28 entri peserta. Daftar pelaksana mencantumkan 7 dosen dan 10 mahasiswa. Jadwal mengalokasikan 30 menit untuk persiapan dan 180 menit untuk edukasi serta distribusi. Rincian pengadaan mencantumkan 2 kg daun sungkai dan 50 wadah tabung. Luaran yang terdokumentasi berupa penyampaian informasi pengolahan dan penyeduhan, pembagian leaflet, serta distribusi produk gratis dalam kemasan berlabel. Koordinasi tim dan dukungan institusi mendukung kegiatan, sedangkan keterbatasan alat peraga dan pengeras suara serta kegiatan kesehatan lain menjadi hambatan. Analisis menunjukkan bahwa kegiatan menyediakan sarana diseminasi herbal di ruang publik dengan menggabungkan komunikasi lisan, media cetak, dan contoh fisik. Jumlah pengadaan belum menggambarkan jumlah produk terdistribusi, dan perubahan pengetahuan belum dapat diukur karena tidak tersedia data evaluasi berpasangan. Program lanjutan perlu memperkuat pencatatan distribusi, praktik pengolahan, serta evaluasi pemahaman dan mutu produk.

title: Endometriosis and microplastics: potential implications for pain symptoms
abstractText: Introduction Endometriosis is an estrogen-dependent, chronic inflammatory condition affecting roughly 10% of reproductive-aged women and is characterized by pelvic pain and infertility. Microplastics are ubiquitous environmental plastic contaminants less than 5 mm in size that have been found in the human body, notably, the female reproductive system. This review addresses the range of endometriosis pelvic pain symptoms, posing microplastics as a potential differentiating environmental factor. Methods We searched PubMed and Google Scholar using search terms endometriosis and microplastics to identify relevant studies as well as reference lists from those publications. Results and Discussion Only one study has measured and compared microplastics in the urine of women with and without endometriosis showing no significant differences in level or type of microplastic, particle sizes were larger and more irregular in those with endometriosis. While microplastics are associated with inflammatory response and dysregulated immune response and have the potential to amplify pathways contributing to pelvic pain, there are no studies that directly demonstrate an association between microplastics and endometriosis or endometriosis-associated pain. More research is needed to clarify the potential impact of microplastics on endometriosis-associated pain, including characterization of microplastics locally (peritoneal fluid, tissue) and systemically (blood), validated pain assessment, and longitudinal follow up to clarify temporality between microplastic exposure and endometriosis.

Electronic Evidence, Authentication Challenges, and the Qarinah Doctrine: Judicial Reasoning in Divorce Cases Involving Alleged Cyber Infidelity at the Batang Religious Court
abstractText: This study examines the legal reasoning of judges at the Batang Religious Court in assessing electronic evidence in the form of printed screenshots of digital conversations in divorce cases involving allegations of cyber infidelity. It focuses on the relationship between the legal recognition of electronic evidence under the Law on Electronic Information and Transactions (EIT Law) and the requirements of authenticity, integrity, and accessibility. This study adopts a normative legal approach and a multiple embedded case study design to examine 16 divorce decisions issued in 2025. The analysis of judicial reasoning focuses on 14 cases decided on the merits, while the remaining two cases provide procedural context. The findings show that Article 19(f) of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975 was the most frequently invoked ground for divorce, although the formulation of the claims varied across cases. Judges treated printed digital evidence as supporting indications rather than as conclusive proof of the allegations. Its assessment was considered alongside witness testimony and other facts established during the proceedings. The study also finds that the subsequent affixing of stamp duty (nazegelen) does not, by itself, establish the authenticity or integrity of the underlying electronic data. The absence of digital forensic verification therefore raises potential evidentiary concerns, particularly when the source, authenticity, or context of the material is disputed. The doctrines of qarīnah and judicial presumptions may provide analytical frameworks for assessing electronic indications, provided that their probative value is evaluated in conjunction with other relevant evidence and the circumstances of each case.

Environmental Enrichment for Early Stroke Rehabilitation: A Systematic Review
abstractText: Stroke remains a leading cause of long-term disability, and the first 12 weeks after stroke represent a period of heightened neuroplasticity during which activity-dependent stimulation may support neurological recovery. Environmental enrichment (EE) has been proposed as a potentially low-cost strategy to increase meaningful physical, cognitive, and social engagement beyond scheduled rehabilitation sessions. However, evidence regarding its effectiveness in early stroke rehabilitation has remained limited. This systematic review aimed to identify, critically appraise, and synthesize comparative evidence on EE during early inpatient stroke rehabilitation, focusing on activity levels, safety, functional recovery, and psychological well-being, while evaluating methodological quality and risk of bias. Four databases—PubMed, ScienceDirect, Europe PMC, and Epistemonikos—were searched, yielding 492 records. Following screening, two nonrandomized controlled studies met the inclusion criteria. Methodological quality was appraised using Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine (OCEBM) critical appraisal worksheets, risk of bias was assessed using the Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated qualitatively according to the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. Both studies reported increased overall, physical, and social activity and reduced inactivity following EE interventions. Improvements appeared greater in acute stroke settings than in subacute rehabilitation, where limited fidelity to individually tailored enrichment protocols may have attenuated intervention effects. Neither study identified an increased risk of adverse events, and one reported fewer adverse events and a shorter hospital length of stay. Neither study demonstrated statistically significant improvements in functional outcomes or quality of life at three months. Overall risk of bias was rated serious in one study and moderate in the other, while certainty of evidence ranged from low to very low across the assessed outcomes. These findings suggested that EE may be a feasible and potentially low-cost adjunct to early inpatient stroke rehabilitation, with benefits for daily activity and engagement. However, the limited evidence did not establish its long-term effectiveness in improving functional recovery or reducing disability.

Recognizing and Responding to Medical Neglect: Clinical Report
abstractText: Medical neglect occurs when a caregiver fails to provide or seek necessary medical care, resulting in harm or risk of harm to a child. This clinical report outlines key diagnostic criteria for medical neglect, emphasizing that medical nonadherence alone does not constitute neglect unless accompanied by (1) harm or risk of harm; (2) significant benefit from recommended care (when care is sought); (3) a favorable risk-benefit ratio; (4) demonstrated accessibility of care; and (5) clear communication of medical advice. Medical neglect disproportionately affects children with chronic conditions, mental health needs, or special health care requirements, while systemic inequities such as poverty, racial disparities, and limited access to care further exacerbate risks. Clinical presentations vary widely, from untreated dental caries to life-threatening exacerbations of chronic illness. A multidisciplinary, family-centered approach is critical to address modifiable barriers including health literacy, transportation needs, and implicit biases while prioritizing the child’s safety. Strategies include enhancing communication, leveraging community resources, and collaborating with child protective services when necessary. This report highlights the pediatrician’s role in advocating for equitable health care access and systemic reforms to reduce disparities. By distinguishing neglect from nonadherence and addressing root causes, providers can mitigate harm and improve outcomes for vulnerable children.

title: DORI VOSITALARI TA'SIRIDA RIVOJLANGAN RINITNI DAVOLASH TAKTIKASINI KONSERVATIV VA LAZER USULIDAGI JARROHLIK KORREKSIYASI NATIJALARINI QIYOSIY BAHOLASH ASOSIDA TAKOMILLASHTIRISH
abstractText: Medikamentoz rinit (rhinitis medicamentosa) — mahalliy qon tomirlarni toraytiruvchi preparatlarni uzoq muddat yoki haddan tashqari ko'p qo'llash natijasida yuzaga keladigan noallergik rinit shaklidir. Ushbu kasallik burun bitishining doimiy tus olishi, dori vositasining ta'siri tugagandan so'ng burun shilliq qavati shishining qayta kuchayishi va hayot sifatining pasayishi bilan kechadi. Tadqiqotning maqsadi Farg'ona viloyatida medikamentoz rinit bilan kasallangan bemorlarda konservativ davolash va lazer yordamida jarrohlik korreksiyasi natijalarini qiyosiy baholashdan iborat. Tadqiqotga medikamentoz rinit bilan kasallangan 86 nafar bemor jalb qilinib, ular 43 nafardan iborat ikki guruhga ajratildi. Birinchi guruhda konservativ davolash usuli qo'llanildi, ikkinchi guruhda esa klinik ko'rsatmalarga muvofiq pastki burun chig'anoqlarini lazer yordamida reduksiya qilish muolajasi zarur dori vositalari bilan davolash bilan birgalikda amalga oshirildi. Olti oydan so'ng konservativ davolash guruhida NOSE ko'rsatkichi 70 balldan 32 ballgacha, lazer yordamida jarrohlik amaliyoti o'tkazilgan guruhda esa 72 balldan 20 ballgacha pasaydi. Burun qon tomirlarini toraytiruvchi preparatlardan to'liq voz kechish birinchi guruhda 31 nafar (72,1%), ikkinchi guruhda esa 39 nafar (90,7%) bemorda qayd etildi. EN Medication-induced rhinitis (rhinitis medicamentosa) is a form of non-allergic rhinitis that develops as a result of prolonged or excessive use of topical vasoconstrictive agents. The condition is characterized by persistent nasal congestion, recurrent swelling of the nasal mucosa after the effects of the medication wear off, and a reduced quality of life. The aim of this study was to compare the outcomes of conservative treatment and laser-assisted surgical correction in patients with medication-induced rhinitis in the Fergana region. The study included 86 patients diagnosed with medication-induced rhinitis, who were divided into two groups of 43 patients each. Patients in Group 1 received conservative treatment, whereas those in Group 2 underwent laser reduction of the inferior nasal turbinates, when clinically indicated, in combination with the necessary pharmacological therapy. After 6 months, the NOSE score decreased from 70 to 32 points in the conservative treatment group and from 72 to 20 points in the laser intervention group. Complete discontinuation of topical vasoconstrictive agents was achieved in 31 patients (72.1%) in Group 1 and 39 patients (90.7%) in Group 2. RU Медикаментозный ринит (rhinitis medicamentosa) — это форма неаллергического ринита, возникающая в результате длительного или чрезмерного применения местных сосудосуживающих препаратов. Заболевание характеризуется постоянной заложенностью носа, повторным усилением отёка слизистой оболочки носа после прекращения действия препарата и снижением качества жизни. Цель исследования — сравнительная оценка результатов консервативного лечения и лазерной хирургической коррекции у пациентов с медикаментозным ринитом в Ферганской области. В исследовании приняли участие 86 пациентов с медикаментозным ринитом, которые были разделены на две группы по 43 человека. Первая группа получала консервативное лечение, а пациентам второй группы по клиническим показаниям проводилась лазерная редукция нижних носовых раковин в сочетании с необходимой медикаментозной терапией. Через 6 месяцев показатель по шкале NOSE снизился с 70 до 32 баллов в группе консервативного лечения и с 72 до 20 баллов в группе лазерного хирургического вмешательства. Полный отказ от применения местных сосудосуживающих препаратов был зарегистрирован у 31 (72,1%) пациента первой группы и у 39 (90,7%) пациентов второй группы.

title: Hubungan Asupan Purin, Aktivitas Fisik, dan Indeks Massa Tubuh dengan Kadar Asam Urat pada Mahasiswa Profesi Dokter Universitas Jambi
abstractText: Hiperurisemia merupakan masalah kesehatan yang kian meningkat pada kelompok usia muda, khususnya mahasiswa profesi dokter yang rentan mengalami perubahan gaya hidup dan pola makan akibat tingginya beban akademik serta rotasi klinik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis hubungan antara asupan purin, aktivitas fisik, dan Indeks Massa Tubuh (IMT) dengan kadar asam urat pada mahasiswa profesi dokter Universitas Jambi. Penelitian ini menggunakan desain kuantitatif observasional analitik dengan pendekatan cross-sectional, penelitian ini melibatkan 113 responden yang dipilih melalui teknik consecutive sampling, di mana data dikumpulkan menggunakan kuesioner terstruktur, pengukuran antropometri,serta alat tes asam urat digital, dan dianalisis menggunakan uji Chi-Square. Adanya hubungan yang signifikan antara asupan purin (p<0,001p<0,001) dan IMT dengan kadar asam urat, sedangkan aktivitas fisik tidak menunjukkan hubungan yang signifikan (p=0,089p=0,089), yang mengimplikasikan bahwa manajemen pola makan dan pengendalian berat badan sangat krusial untuk menekan risiko gangguan metabolik sejak dini serta menjadi landasan bagi kebijakan promotif dan preventif dalam praktik kesehatan di lingkungan pendidikan kedokteran. Asupan purin dan IMT terbukti berhubungan secara signifikan dengan kadar asam urat pada mahasiswa profesi dokter, sehingga direkomendasikan perlunya peningkatan edukasi gizi dan intervensi gaya hidup sehat secara berkesinambungan untuk pencegahan jangka panjang.

title: Thoracic wall fascial plane blocks (pectoral nerve and serratus anterior plane blocks) versus thoracic paravertebral block in patients undergoing breast surgery: a systematic review, meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis of analgesic effects
abstractText: Abstract Background Thoracic wall fascial plane blocks, principally the pectoral nerve (PECS I/II) and serratus anterior plane (SAPB) blocks, and the thoracic paravertebral block (PVB) are both used to provide analgesia for breast surgery, but they have not been formally compared in a contemporary quantitative synthesis. We compared their effects on postoperative resting pain scores, 24 h morphine equivalent consumption, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), time to first rescue analgesia and reported block-related complications. Methods Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing a thoracic wall fascial plane block (FPB; PECS I, PECS II, SAPB or pecto-intercostal fascial block) with PVB in adults undergoing breast surgery were identified from PubMed, EMBASE, Google Scholar, the Cochrane Library and ClinicalTrials.gov to March 2025. Two investigators independently screened studies and extracted data. All continuous outcomes were expressed in clinically interpretable units (pain on a common 0–10 scale, opioid consumption as intravenous morphine equivalents in mg, and time to first rescue analgesia in hours) and were pooled as mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI); standardised mean differences (SMD) are reported as sensitivity analyses. Dichotomous outcomes were pooled as odds ratios (OR). Random-effects models used restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimation of the between-study variance with the Hartung–Knapp adjustment, and 95% prediction intervals are reported alongside confidence intervals. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane tool and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Subgroup analyses (PECS versus SAPB; mastectomy versus non-mastectomy surgery), sensitivity analyses excluding trials at high risk of bias, and trial sequential analyses (TSA) were performed. Results A total of 21 RCTs involving 1167 patients were included. Resting pain scores were lower after FPB than after PVB at 6 h [MD 0.50 points, 95% CI 0.14–0.85; I² = 75%], the only outcome to reach statistical significance in the revised primary analyses. At 0 h, a post hoc timepoint not listed in the registered protocol, the difference was no longer statistically significant once the Hartung–Knapp correction was applied [MD 0.41 points, 95% CI − 0.02–0.83; I² = 88%], whereas the original DerSimonian–Laird analysis had reached significance. Both point estimates lie below the 1.0-point threshold for a clinically important difference, and the 95% prediction intervals for both timepoints ( − 0.97–1.79 and −0.60–1.59 points) include no difference in either direction. No statistically significant differences were found in 24 h IV morphine equivalent requirements [MD 1.14 mg, 95% CI − 0.64–2.91], resting pain scores at 2 h [MD 0.30 points, 95% CI − 0.16–0.76], 12 h [MD 0.33 points, 95% CI − 0.26–0.93] or 24 h [MD − 0.20 points, 95% CI − 0.63–0.23], time to first rescue analgesia [MD − 1.73 h, 95% CI − 3.60–0.13], or PONV [OR 1.44, 95% CI 0.89–2.34]; for each of these outcomes the confidence interval crossed the null value, so the direction of any difference is uncertain. After exclusion of the five trials at high risk of bias, the difference at 6 h [MD 0.37 points, 95% CI − 0.06–0.80] was no longer statistically significant. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested that the early differences were confined to PECS rather than SAPB trials, but only one of eight tests for subgroup interaction was statistically significant. After reassessment of imprecision against prespecified thresholds for clinically important benefit and harm, certainty of evidence was low for four outcomes (resting pain at 0, 2 and 6 h and PONV) and very low for the remaining four (24 h morphine equivalent consumption, resting pain at 12 and 24 h, and time to first rescue analgesia); no outcome was rated moderate or high. Pneumothorax was reported in two PVB patients and in no FPB patient, and no case of local anaesthetic systemic toxicity was reported. Conclusion Thoracic wall fascial plane blocks may be associated with slightly lower resting pain scores than PVB at 6 h, but the entire confidence interval lies below the 1.0-point threshold for a clinically important difference, so the evidence is compatible only with an effect too small to matter to patients; the certainty of this evidence is low, and the difference did not persist after exclusion of trials at high risk of bias. The apparent difference at 0 h did not survive an appropriate random-effects correction and arose at a post hoc timepoint. Trial sequential analyses are exploratory and do not indicate that these findings are unlikely to change with further evidence. No consistent differences were found in 24 h opioid consumption, later pain scores, time to first rescue analgesia or PONV. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested possible differences between PECS and SAPB that require confirmation in adequately powered, standardised trials conducted within contemporary multimodal analgesia pathways. Available safety data were too sparse to establish comparative safety. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/ . (PROSPERO), identifier CRD 42024597114

Impact of invasive fungal disease on outcomes in adult allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation: a post-hoc analysis from a nationwide Polish Adult Leukemia Group study
abstractText: Abstract The present analysis is based on a retrospective cross-sectional Polish study including patients who underwent allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT) over a 3-year period (2012–2014). The aim of the study was to evaluate the impact of the updated 2019 invasive fungal disease (IFD) diagnostic criteria on treatment outcomes and to identify risk factors for mortality. The analysis included 102 patients diagnosed with IFD for whom follow-up data were available. In accordance with the 2019 EORTC/MSGERC consensus revisions, all IFD diagnoses were re-evaluated using the available clinical data. Additionally, due to the lack of therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM), patients receiving oral posaconazole suspension who presented with multiple risk factors for IFD and radiological findings on high-resolution chest computed tomography (HRCT) suggestive of fungal infection were classified as probable IFD cases, even in the presence of negative serum galactomannan (GM) results. Using the 2008 EORTC/MSG criteria, 3-month mortality rates were comparable between patients with probable and proven IFD (47.4% and 50%, respectively) and lower among patients classified as possible IFD (27.9%). In contrast, application of the modified 2019 IFD definitions resulted in a clearer stratification of patients into possible, probable, and proven IFD categories, with distinct 3-month mortality rates of 16%, 36%, and 52.4%, respectively. In multivariate analysis, neutropenia occurring at any time after transplantation – a major risk factor for IFD development – was independently associated with increased mortality. Moreover, proven IFD diagnosed according to the updated criteria significantly increased the risk of IFD-related death. In conclusion, reclassification of IFD according to updated criteria and adjustment for historical diagnostic limitations improved prognostic stratification, yielding clinically meaningful differences in mortality among possible, probable, and proven IFD cases.

ATIVIDADES PROFISSIONAIS QUE EXIGEM PRODUTIVIDADE E CUMPRIMENTO DE METAS: UMA ANÁLISE SOBRE A SAÚDE MENTAL DO TRABALHADOR E A RESPONSABILIDADE DO EMPREGADOR
abstractText: O presente trabalho analisa os impactos do sistema das atividades que exigem produtividade e cumprimento de metas, observando-se o dano causado a saúde mental do trabalhador, bem como a responsabilização do empregador. Tal fator é impulsionado pela globalização, pelos avanços tecnológicos e pela competitividade no mercado, o que faz com que as empresas adotem modelos inadequados de gestão, em que o desempenho do funcionário passa a ser avaliado através dos cumprimentos de metas cada vez mais severas e inalcançáveis, no qual a busca pela eficiência e produtividade passou a ocupar posição central nas estratégias empresariais. Embora estes mecanismos sejam necessários para o funcionamento e organização do trabalho, quando aplicado de maneira desproporcional, pode comprometer a saúde mental dos trabalhadores, e, consequentemente originar transtornos psicológicos relacionados ao ambiente de trabalho. Com o aumento da incidência de transtornos mentais, como a ansiedade, depressão, síndrome de burnout e estresse ocupacional, a saúde mental passou a ser tema de relevância para o ordenamento jurídico brasileiro, pois a evolução legislativa e doutrinária demonstra que a tutela da integridade do trabalhador não se restringe à prevenção de acidentes e doenças físicas, abrangendo também os riscos psicossociais decorrentes da organização do trabalho, da pressão por resultados, da sobrecarga de atividades e das práticas de gestão que favorecem ambientes laborais hostis. Nesse contexto, a recente atualização da Norma Regulamentadora nº 1 (NR-1), ao incluir expressamente os fatores de risco psicossociais no Gerenciamento de Riscos Ocupacionais, reforçou o dever do empregador de identificar, avaliar e prevenir situações capazes de comprometer a saúde mental dos empregados.

A CONTRIBUIÇÃO DA METODOLOGIA 5S PARA A ORGANIZAÇÃO, SEGURANÇA E EFICIÊNCIA OPERACIONAL EM AMBIENTES INDUSTRIAIS
abstractText: Os ambientes industriais exigem organização dos recursos, controle das condições de trabalho e redução de perdas que afetam o desempenho operacional. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar a contribuição da metodologia 5S para a organização, a segurança e a eficiência operacional em ambientes industriais, com atenção às condições associadas à manutenção dos resultados. Foi realizada uma revisão integrativa, de abordagem qualitativa e finalidade descritiva, com buscas no Google Acadêmico, Scopus, ScienceDirect e SciELO, contemplando publicações de 2021 a junho de 2026. Foram identificados 186 registros; após remoção de 42 duplicados e aplicação dos critérios de triagem e elegibilidade, 24 artigos compuseram a amostra final. Os resultados foram agrupados em cinco dimensões, segundo critérios de codificação baseados em resultados explícitos, quantitativos ou qualitativos. As contribuições mais recorrentes envolveram organização do espaço, eficiência operacional, segurança, qualidade e padronização. A manutenção dos resultados foi associada a treinamento, auditorias periódicas, participação dos trabalhadores, acompanhamento gerencial, indicadores e revisão dos padrões. Conclui-se que a literatura apresenta ganhos mensurados e benefícios descritivos, mas as diferenças metodológicas e a limitada avaliação longitudinal impedem atribuir causalidade ou assegurar a permanência dos resultados.

title: Towards Dialogic Teaching in Primary School Science: Exploring Teacher-Student Talks in Classifying Materials
abstractText: This study aims to examine the effectiveness of dialogic teaching in supporting Year 4 students’ learning of classifying materials in primary science, with particular attention to their use of first language (L1) and second language (L2) during classroom dialogue. A convenience sample of 20 Year 4 students from a government school in Brunei Darussalam participated in the study. Data were collected through pre-test and post-test measures, video recordings, and classroom observations and analyzed using a paired-samples t-test and thematic content analysis. The findings showed that dialogic teaching improved students’ performance in classifying materials. Students generally provided shorter responses when using English (L2), while Malay (L1) also facilitated participation in classroom dialogue. Responses tended to be longer when students combined L1 and L2 and received teacher prompts. However, balancing L1 and L2 use remained challenging for sustaining dialogic interaction. The findings suggest that strategically integrating students’ L1 with English can support participation in dialogic primary science learning, particularly by accommodating differences in English proficiency and reducing vocabulary-related barriers to classroom interaction. Keywords: dialogic teaching, primary school science, classroom communicative approaches, prompts.

title: Reclaiming The City of Gold’s story through graphic design as narrative infrastructure for inclusive and circular placemaking in Johannesburg
abstractText: Purpose This paper aims to explore how collaborative graphic design pedagogy may contribute conceptually to inclusive and circular placemaking in a contested Johannesburg heritage precinct. It interprets speculative visual communication proposals as potential narrative infrastructure and develops symbolic circularity as a cultural and communicative complement to material circularity. Design/methodology/approach The research uses an interpretive, research-through-design case of an honours service-learning unit conducted with a local non-profit organisation. The corpus comprises student design artefacts, studio observations, walking-based visual documentation and formative feedback. Artefacts were interpreted through three propositions: gathering multiple narratives, continuity rather than replacement and collective authorship. The proposals were not implemented or evaluated with everyday precinct users. Findings The proposals most clearly support continuity rather than replacement through the reuse and recoding of Art Deco geometry and inherited visual references. They show conceptual potential for gathering multiple narratives through adaptable identity, wayfinding and projected-content systems. Collective authorship is least substantiated because participation was limited to the partner organisation and final design control remained with student teams. Digital access, curation, governance, maintenance and long-term stewardship remain unresolved. Originality/value The paper offers an exploratory theoretical contribution by defining symbolic circularity as the intentional reuse, recoding and circulation of inherited cultural meanings through graphic and narrative intervention. It positions narrative infrastructure as a potential basis for future participatory placemaking, while distinguishing speculative design capacity from enacted participation, environmental performance and realised urban impact.

title: Students’ engagement and perceived effectiveness of Wordwall activities for ESL sentence construction
abstractText: This study investigated students' behavioural, emotional and cognitive engagement, and their perceived effectiveness of Wordwall, following the use of Wordwall activities in English sentence construction lessons in one secondary school in Malaysia. While digital and game-based learning are gaining traction in the language classroom, constructing sentences can be a challenge for language learners and may need to be practised multiple times with feedback and active engagement. A quantitative descriptive survey design was employed with 55 Form 1 and Form 2 students from four classes in one secondary school in Malaysia. The participants engaged in three Wordwall-based sentence construction sessions followed by a post-intervention questionnaire that measured behavioural, emotional and cognitive engagement and the perceived effectiveness of Wordwall. The data were analysed using frequencies, means, standard deviations and Cronbach's alpha to assess the internal consistency of the questionnaire scales. The results showed that self-reported engagement scores were moderately positive across all three dimensions, with emotional engagement recording the highest mean score (M = 3.45, SD = 0.85), followed by cognitive engagement (M = 3.42, SD = 0.82) and behavioural engagement (M = 3.34, SD = 0.84); however, differences among the three dimensions were small. Students also reported moderately positive perceptions of the effectiveness of Wordwall for learning sentence construction (M = 3.28, SD = 1.09). These findings suggest that Wordwall may serve as a supplementary tool in interactive and participatory sentence construction lessons. However, the study did not measure learning gains, no control group was used, and the small convenience sample limits generalisation; the results therefore reflect students' self-reported perceptions only. Future research should incorporate objective measures of learning and stronger comparative designs in ESL classrooms. Kajian ini meneliti penglibatan tingkah laku, emosi dan kognitif pelajar serta persepsi mereka terhadap keberkesanan Wordwall susulan penggunaan aktiviti Wordwall dalam pengajaran pembinaan ayat bahasa Inggeris di sebuah sekolah menengah di Malaysia. Walaupun pembelajaran digital dan pembelajaran berasaskan permainan semakin mendapat tempat dalam bilik darjah bahasa, pembinaan ayat boleh menjadi cabaran kepada pelajar dan mungkin memerlukan latihan berulang dengan maklum balas serta penglibatan aktif. Reka bentuk tinjauan deskriptif kuantitatif digunakan melibatkan 55 orang pelajar Tingkatan 1 dan Tingkatan 2 daripada empat kelas di sebuah sekolah menengah di Malaysia. Peserta kajian mengambil bahagian dalam tiga sesi pembinaan ayat berasaskan Wordwall yang diikuti dengan soal selidik pascaintervensi untuk mengukur penglibatan tingkah laku, emosi dan kognitif serta persepsi terhadap keberkesanan Wordwall. Data dianalisis menggunakan kekerapan, min, sisihan piawai dan alfa Cronbach bagi menilai ketekalan dalaman skala soal selidik tersebut. Dapatan kajian menunjukkan bahawa skor penglibatan yang dilaporkan sendiri oleh pelajar berada pada tahap sederhana positif merentasi ketiga-tiga dimensi, dengan penglibatan emosi mencatatkan skor min tertinggi (M = 3.45, SD = 0.85), diikuti oleh penglibatan kognitif (M = 3.42, SD = 0.82) dan penglibatan tingkah laku (M = 3.34, SD = 0.84). Walau bagaimanapun, perbezaan antara ketiga-tiga dimensi tersebut adalah kecil. Pelajar juga melaporkan persepsi yang sederhana positif terhadap keberkesanan Wordwall dalam pembelajaran pembinaan ayat (M = 3.28, SD = 1.09). Dapatan ini menunjukkan bahawa Wordwall berpotensi digunakan sebagai alat sokongan dalam pengajaran pembinaan ayat secara interaktif dan melibatkan penyertaan aktif pelajar. Namun demikian, kajian ini tidak mengukur peningkatan hasil pembelajaran, tiada kumpulan kawalan digunakan, dan saiz sampel mudah yang kecil membataskan kebolehumuman dapatan. Oleh itu, dapatan kajian ini hanya mencerminkan persepsi yang dilaporkan sendiri oleh pelajar. Kajian pada masa hadapan wajar menggunakan pengukuran hasil pembelajaran secara objektif serta reka bentuk kajian perbandingan yang lebih kukuh dalam bilik darjah bahasa Inggeris sebagai bahasa kedua (ESL).

title: Bridging the gap in One Health: challenges at the diagnostic interface – laboratory insights on sample quality and stewardship
abstractText: Abstract Background The aim was to conduct an interface analysis to assess the sources and frequency of errors in the diagnostic workflows involved in handling human and animal microbiological samples. Methods A web-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among German-speaking healthcare workers in human and veterinary medicine between 7th October 2022 and 14th July 2023. The data evaluated in this study focus on perceptions of microbiology laboratory staff responsible for specimen reception, processing, and interpretation (sample recipients, SR) in human and veterinary laboratories across both outpatient and inpatient settings in German-speaking countries. Based on the questionnaire sent out using the snowball method, 20 of the 166 questions were tailored to recipients of diagnostics and used for descriptive and statistical (t-tests, chi-square tests) data analysis. Results A total of 2,464 valid responses were analysed; 372 (15.1%) were identified as SR, with the largest group working in human medicine (HM) (n=166, 44.6%). Respondents estimated that 18.5 samples per 100 were incorrectly requested by HM, compared with 15.4 by veterinarians and 14.8 by medical technicians (MT). All professional groups consistently cited swabs as the most error-prone material. Respondents with over 10 years of experience more frequently reported that requests took over 60 minutes of post-processing time per day. However, this was not statistically significant. Conclusions SR face substantial challenges due to insufficient information, communication gaps, and inconsistent sample quality. Effective diagnostic stewardship requires addressing these issues through interprofessional education, digital decision-support, and standardised test-requesting processes.

title: Pharmacologic Management of Pediatric Paroxysmal Sympathetic Hyperactivity in North America
abstractText: OBJECTIVE Describe pharmacological management approaches to pediatric paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity (PSH) among North American pediatric attending physicians. PARTICIPANTS AND METHODS Cross-sectional web-based survey of pediatric attending physicians conducted from March to August 2023. The questionnaire examined PSH medication utilization and preferences, subspecialty responsibilities for managing PSH, and the influence of patient age on medication selection. Descriptive statistics summarize PSH medication utilization and rank-order preferences. Chi-square analyses examined relationships between physician specialty and medication selection. RESULTS Among 295 respondents (33% palliative care, 23% neurology, 18% complex care, 17% physiatry), considerable heterogeneity in PSH pharmacotherapy approaches was observed. The most used abortive PSH medications were gamma-aminobutyric acid A (GABA-A) agonists (86%), alpha-2 agonists (79%), and opioids (49%). Leading preventive PSH medications included alpha-2 agonists (90%), gabapentinoids (89%), and beta-blockers (66%). Top-ranked medications for abortive management were alpha-2 agonists, GABA-A agonists, and non-opioid analgesics; and gabapentinoids, alpha-2 agonists, and beta-blockers for preventive management. While physiatrists and neurologists were most frequently identified as primary managers of PSH at participants’ home institutions, several other specialties (including multidisciplinary models) were reported as well. We observed significant differences in utilization of alpha-2 agonists, opioids, dopamine agonists, and beta-blockers across subspecialties (all P < .05). Patient age influenced medication selection among 41% of our sample. CONCLUSIONS Pharmacologic management of pediatric PSH currently lacks clinical consensus and varies significantly based on physician subspecialty. Our findings underscore the need for focused research efforts to identify optimal treatment strategies and develop standardized and evidence-based management guidelines.

title: Deubiquitinase USP14 restrains autophagy via LARS/mTORC1 axis to accelerate apoptosis in intervertebral disc degeneration
abstractText: Abstract Nutrient deficiency is a key contributor to the pathogenesis of intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD), exacerbating nucleus pulposus (NP) cell apoptosis and extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation. Here, we identified ubiquitin-specific protease 14 (USP14) as a critical stress-responsive regulator that is amplified in human and rat degenerative NP tissues. USP14 upregulation exacerbates nutrient deprivation–induced apoptosis and ECM degradation by inhibiting protective autophagy. Mechanistically, USP14 directly interacts with leucyl-tRNA synthetase (LARS) via its C-terminal catalytic domain, catalyzing the removal of K48-linked polyubiquitin chains to prevent proteasomal degradation of LARS. LARS stabilization hyperactivates the mTORC1 pathway, leading to autophagy suppression. The essential role of autophagy inhibition in USP14-mediated pathology was confirmed when pharmacological (chloroquine) or genetic (ATG5 siRNA) blockade of autophagy abolished the protective effects of USP14 knockdown. Both genetic targeting (siRNA, catalytic mutant C114A) and pharmacological inhibition (IU-1) of USP14 suppressed LARS/mTORC1 overactivation, restored autophagic flux, and mitigated NP cell damage, whereas LARS silencing or mTORC1 inhibition (rapamycin) alleviated USP14-driven pathological effects. Notably, intradiscal IU-1 delivery in a rat model of IDD attenuated disc degeneration, decreased apoptosis, and enhanced autophagic activity. Thus, we identified the USP14/LARS/mTORC1 axis as a ubiquitination-controlled mechanism regulating the autophagy-apoptosis equilibrium in nutrient-stressed NP cells, establishing USP14 as a promising therapeutic target for IDD.

Predictive Auto Scaling and Cloud Cost Optimization Using Machine Learning
abstractText: Cloud applications experience fluctuating demand, requiring resource controllers to balance infrastructure cost against service performance. Reactive autoscaling changes capacity after monitored utilization crosses a threshold; predictive autoscaling attempts to provision resources before demand materializes. This paper evaluates a machine-learning-assisted autoscaling approach using a reproducible synthetic workload benchmark. A deterministic generator produces 40,000 five-minute observations with daily and weekly seasonality, autoregressive variation, noise, and burst events. Historical lag and rolling-window features support a 15-minute-ahead request-demand forecast. Persistence, Random Forest, histogram-based gradient boosting, and XGBoost are considered, with chronological train, validation, and test partitions. Across five random seeds, XGBoost obtains mean absolute error of 163.87 requests (standard deviation 1.97), root mean squared error of 208.83 (4.35), and coefficient of determination of 0.7373 (0.0086). In a separate single-seed controller replay, predictive scaling reduces normalized instance-hour cost by approximately 0.29% relative to a reactive threshold policy. However, the fraction of intervals above the 70% CPU proxy rises from 2.70% to 4.39%. These results show that forecast accuracy alone does not guarantee operational improvement. The benchmark is synthetic, cost is normalized, and CPU thresholds are not application-level service-level objectives. Real-trace validation and latency-aware queue simulation remain necessary before production conclusions can be drawn.

title: K/Ce/Sm multiple-doped CaBi 2 Nb 2 O 9 aurivillius-type ceramics used for high-temperature piezoelectric ultrasonic transducer
abstractText: Abstract Aurivillius-type CaBi2Nb2O9 (CBN) is attractive for high-temperature ultrasonic sensing owing to its high Curie temperature (TC ≈ 940 ℃). However, its weak piezoelectric response and loss of polarization alignment during thermal exposure limit its practical performance. Herein, K/Ce/Sm co-substitution at the Ca site was employed to modify the lattice structure, electrical transport, and domain morphology of CBN ceramics. Co-substitution reduced the orthorhombic distortion while preserving the orthorhombic framework. The optimized CBN-KCS-12 ceramic exhibited a piezoelectric coefficient d33 of 18 pC/N, a TC of approximately 933 ℃, and a ρdc resistivity of 2.59 × 106 Ω·cm at 650 ℃, approximately 18.5 times that of undoped CBN. The annealing temperature corresponding to 50% retention of the initial d₃₃ increased from 600 to 850 ℃, and CBN-KCS-12 retained approximately 44% of its initial d33 after annealing at 900 ℃. Piezoresponse force microscopy revealed larger block-like regions in CBN-KCS-12 compared with the fine stripe-like patterns in undoped CBN, with block-like contrast also observed after annealing at 900 ℃. The elastic modulus also increased from 30.1 to 33.8 GPa. Finally, a single-element ultrasonic transducer fabricated from CBN-KCS-12 produced clear pulse-echo signals from room temperature to 400 ℃, achieving a signal-to-noise ratio above 36 dB and a -6 dB fractional bandwidth of approximately 42% at 400 °C. These results demonstrate the potential of multi-element A-site co-substitution for improving CBN ceramics for high-temperature ultrasonic applications.

title: Perceived workplace discrimination and its impacts on leaders: latent class analysis
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to identify distinct latent classes of perceived workplace discrimination among leaders and examine how different patterns of discrimination perception are associated with workplace attitudes and behaviors. Design/methodology/approach Using a mixture modeling approach, this study conducted latent class analysis with data from 3,351 leaders drawn from the 2022 Korean Women Manager Panel. The study examined predictors of latent class membership, including shadow labor culture, fairness of HR practices and top management leadership and compared organizational outcomes across the identified classes. Findings The findings revealed five distinct latent classes representing heterogeneous patterns of perceived workplace discrimination among leaders. The results demonstrated that organizational contextual factors significantly differentiated class membership. In addition, significant differences were found across the latent classes in organizational satisfaction and organizational commitment. However, leadership efficacy did not significantly differ across classes, suggesting that perceived workplace discrimination may influence organizational attitudes more strongly than leaders’ self-perceived leadership capability. Originality/value This study contributes to the human resource development and workplace discrimination literature by shifting attention from directly experienced discrimination to leaders’ perceived workplace discrimination as a socially constructed and organizationally embedded phenomenon. The study also extends existing research by demonstrating that perceptions of workplace discrimination are multidimensional rather than continuous and homogeneous. Furthermore, the findings provide practical implications for developing differentiated HRD and organizational interventions aimed at fostering inclusive and supportive workplace environments for leaders.

abstractText: Abstract Purpose-built sexual health chatbots offer young adults anonymous, clinically vetted information, yet sustained adoption remains low, and general-purpose large language models (LLMs) now compete for the same information-seeking moments without comparable safety assurances. This study extended the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) with three domain-specific constructs (trust, privacy concerns, and eHealth literacy) to explain young adults’ behavioral intentions to use sexual health chatbots. College students at a single U.S. university ( N = 216, ages 18 to 24) interacted with Planned Parenthood’s chatbot Roo before completing a survey. Multiple regression explained 40.3% of variance in behavioral intention. Trust in chatbot-provided information was the strongest observed predictor, followed by performance expectancy. Effort expectancy correlated positively with intention at the bivariate level but carried a small, borderline negative partial coefficient in the full model, a pattern consistent with suppression: near-ceiling ease of use added little unique explanatory value once credibility and usefulness were accounted for. Facilitating conditions, privacy concerns, and eHealth literacy were nonsignificant, though exploratory moderation analysis suggested that eHealth literacy may amplify the translation of perceived usefulness into intention. Results were robust to demographic covariates. Participants evaluated the chatbot favorably but reported weak intentions of routine use, an evaluation-adoption gap consistent with episodic, need-driven engagement. Findings identify trust as the strongest factor associated with intentions to use a purpose-built sexual health chatbot. Although general-purpose LLMs were not directly examined, these findings offer design implications for purpose-built chatbots operating in an information environment increasingly dominated by LLMs.

title: Hubungan Derajat Neuropati Perifer dengan Tingkat Keparahan Ulkus Kaki Diabetik yang Menjalani Debridement
abstractText: Neuropati perifer dan ulkus kaki diabetik merupakan komplikasi penting diabetes melitus, tetapi pola hubungan tingkat keparahannya pada pasien yang menjalani debridement perlu dinilai berdasarkan data klinis. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan derajat neuropati perifer dengan keparahan ulkus menurut Wagner di RSU Royal Prima Medan. Rancangan potong lintang retrospektif menggunakan 83 rekam medis yang dipilih secara purposif dari 105 pasien yang menjalani debridement pada 2025. Derajat neuropati dan kategori Wagner diambil dari catatan klinis, kemudian dianalisis melalui distribusi frekuensi, tabulasi silang, dan uji Pearson Chi-Square. Kelompok usia terbanyak adalah 41–60 tahun (50,6%) dan 57,8% pasien berjenis kelamin laki-laki. Neuropati Grade 3 paling sering ditemukan (50,6%), sedangkan kategori ulkus terbanyak ialah Wagner Grade 3 (47,0%). Pada kelompok neuropati Grade 3, sebanyak 57,1% berada pada Wagner Grade 4–5. Tabulasi menunjukkan hubungan yang bermakna secara statistik (χ² = 50,38; p < 0,001), walaupun beberapa sel memiliki frekuensi harapan kecil sehingga perlu pemeriksaan dengan uji eksak. Temuan ini mendukung pentingnya penilaian neuropati bersama evaluasi ulkus secara menyeluruh, tanpa membuktikan sebab-akibat. Penelitian prospektif multisenter dengan penilaian terstandar dan pengendalian faktor perancu dianjurkan untuk memperkuat hasil.

Molecular mechanisms of male sterility in maize and genome editing-based precision design of hybrid seed production systems
abstractText: Male sterility is central to modern maize hybrid seed production because it removes the need for manual emasculation, a labor-intensive and increasingly unscalable practice. This review critically synthesizes the molecular basis of cytoplasmic male sterility (CMS) and genic male sterility (GMS) in maize, focusing on mitochondrial-nuclear genome interaction, tapetal metabolic and developmental disruption, and the additional environmental sensitivity of genic systems (EGMS). In CMS, chimeric mitochondrial open reading frames impair mitochondrial energy metabolism, elevate reactive oxygen species (ROS), and trigger premature tapetal programmed cell death (PCD); nuclear pentatricopeptide-repeat (PPR) restorer-of-fertility (Rf) genes reverse this phenotype in a cytotype- and background-dependent manner. In GMS, hierarchical bHLH and MYB transcription-factor networks direct tapetal differentiation and sporopollenin biosynthesis by integrating lipid and carbohydrate metabolism, hormone signaling, and small-RNA pathways; in EGMS, these networks are further gated by temperature, photoperiod, and protein-quality-control mechanisms. IT is evaluated that genome-editing and synthetic-biology strategies for building precise, scalable sterility systems, distinguishing evidence by validation level. CRISPR/Cas9 is delivered as a transgenic cassette (Cas9, guide RNA and, usually, selectable or visual markers), so edited plants are transgenic until the cassette is removed by genetic segregation or avoided by transient or ribonucleoprotein delivery, and transgene-free status has to be confirmed molecularly rather than assumed. On that basis, knockouts of single-copy and redundant GMS genes are now routinely obtained as cassette-free sterile lines, whereas systems that propagate sterile lines through a maintainer (the ZmMs7-based multi-control sterility system and the RUBY-marked all-in-one seed production technology, ASPT) deliberately retain transgenic reporter or selectable-marker cassettes in the maintainer line, and the gibberellin-switchable ZmKO1 system avoids a marker by using a chemical switch. These systems have been validated across multiple genetic backgrounds and field environments, with hybrid-seed purity above 99% and automated sorting accuracy above 99.8% reported in the cited primary studies, but their regulatory treatment differs according to whether a transgenic maintainer is involved. Beyond male sterility, it is assesed that synthetic apomixis as a prospective “one-line” alternative to the conventional heterotic (two- or three-line) system. In the conventional system, heterosis is expressed in the F1 only: segregation and recombination in the F2 and later generations break up the heterozygous allele combinations (the F2 retains, on average, half of the F1 heterozygosity), so F1 seed must be produced afresh every season by crossing two separately maintained parents in an isolated field, which requires about two seasons per seed lot when parental stocks must first be increased, careful flowering synchrony, and male rows that occupy roughly 20%–33% of the field. In a one-line system, the F1 genotype is propagated through clonal seed (meiosis replaced by mitosis, with parthenogenetic embryo development), so that the hybrid itself is the only line to be multiplied. Mechanism-based estimates (Section 5.3) suggest that this removes the annual cross and sterility maintenance, could save up to one season of lead time per seed lot, and increases the seed-bearing area of a field by 25%–50%. These are projections: more than 95% clonal seed has been reported in an F1 hybrid of rice, whereas no apomictic maize exists, and each hybrid would still have to be created, converted, and tested once. Artificial intelligence (AI)-guided prediction of restorer compatibility is treated separately from apomixis: it is proposed to support the design of sterility and restoration systems and remains exploratory, with no validated, field-deployed maize application. We close by comparing CMS, GMS, and EGMS systematically on mechanism, restoration route, environmental stability, and field readiness, and by discussing the regulatory, intellectual-property, and germplasm-diversity considerations that will determine whether engineered male-sterility systems can be deployed sustainably in maize breeding.

title: Exploiting Low Scanwidth to Resolve Soft Polytomies
abstractText: Phylogenetic networks allow modeling reticulate evolution, capturing events such as hybridization and horizontal gene transfer. A fundamental computational problem in this context is the Tree Containment problem, which asks whether a given phylogenetic network is compatible with a given phylogenetic tree. However, the classical statement of the problem is not robust to poorly supported branches in biological data, possibly leading to false negatives. In an effort to address this, a relaxed version that accounts for uncertainty, called Soft Tree Containment, has been introduced by Bentert, Malík, and Weller [SWAT'18]. We present an algorithm that solves Soft Tree Containment in $2^{O(Δ_T \cdot k \cdot \log(k))} \cdot n^{O(1)}$ time, where $k = \operatorname{sw}(Γ) + Δ_N$, with $Δ_T$ and $Δ_N$ denoting the maximum out-degrees in the tree and the network, respectively, and $\operatorname{sw}(Γ)$ denoting the "scanwidth" [Berry, Scornavacca, and Weller, SOFSEM'20] of a given tree extension of the network, while $n$ is the input size. Our approach leverages the fact that phylogenetic networks encountered in practice often exhibit low scanwidth, making the problem more tractable.

title: Tobacco Product Cancer Risk Perceptions Among Emerging Adults: An Explanatory Sequential Mixed-Methods Study to Inform Cancer Education
abstractText: Abstract Emerging adults navigate a rapidly changing tobacco landscape in which familiar cigarette harms coexist with uncertainty about newer products. Guided by an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, we integrated Health Information National Trends Survey 6 (HINTS 6) data from 476 adults aged 18–29 years with interviews involving 20 emerging adults. Survey-weighted comparisons and adjusted logistic regression examined tobacco-use history, warning awareness, and cancer-related beliefs; thematic analysis explored how participants understood product risks and encountered tobacco-related messages. Ever cigarette/e-cigarette users reported greater cigarette-pack warning awareness than never users (37.8% vs. 12.9%); the adjusted association was imprecise under the multiple-testing criterion. Other group differences in cancer-risk perceptions were not statistically established. Interviews revealed that participants could recognize cancer and addiction risks while viewing vaping as less harsh or more socially acceptable, questioning long-term consequences, and locating tobacco use within peer and marketing environments. Integrating both strands suggests that cancer education should move beyond general risk awareness to address comparative harm, uncertainty, social context, and the credibility of information. These formative findings provide priorities for developing and testing cancer education approaches tailored to emerging adults.
